newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares end lower in sluggish trade.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares end lower in sluggish trade.

text.p: Jakarta share prices ended lower on Thursday as many players were focusing on the year' largest public offer, a partial float of state-owned Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 0.83 points, or 0.15 percent, to close at 568.03 points after rising to 570.26 points earlier in the day. Gainers led losers by 54 to 41, with 68 counters unchanged.
Brokers said they believed the market was likely to continue being sluggish on Friday as it lacked direction and trade was dominated by the BNI offer.

BNI will float around 1.1 billion shares on the Jakarta and Surabaya exhanges at an offer price of 850 rupiah per share. The four-day offer period will start on November 4 and is likely to raise about 922 billion rupiah.

"Some counters are likely to be active tomorrow but volumes will be limited. Some investors have started to collect some good stocks which have been undervalued due to recent weak market sentiment," said one foreign broker.
Secondaries including fisheries firm PT Daya Guna Samudra, property firm Ciputra Development and marble producer Citatah were among the active stocks on Thursday, brokers said.

Daya Guna topped the active list with 7.5 million shares changing hands, rising 25 rupiah to 2,275 rupiah but off a high of 2,325 rupiah. Brokers said the buying was because of good fundamentals coupled with its encouraging debut last week.
Shipping firm Rig Tender finished unchanged at 1,700 on a volume of 1.9 million shares after reaching 1,775 rupiah in late trading.
Brokers said profit-taking eroded earlier gains recorded on market talk of a possible alliance with a foreign partner.
PT Ciputra Development rose 100 rupiah to 1,700 rupiah on a volume of 1.5 million shares. PT Citatah rose 100 rupiah to 1,750 on a volume of 982,000 shares.
"Those stocks are good stocks and prevailing prices were low. So technically, it is a good time to buy," said one local broker.
